title: Peripheral artery disease: stage, side and ulcer
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's peripheral artery disease and any related ulcer.
note:
Chief Complaint
Claudication in the right leg.

HPI
The patient is a 77-year-old woman presenting for evaluation of symptoms related to atherosclerosis. She reports experiencing significant calf pain specifically when walking for moderate distances. She notes that the discomfort occurs consistently in the right leg during exertion and resolves with rest. She denies any nocturnal pain or discomfort while at rest. She also denies any skin breakdown or changes to the integrity of the skin. The patient notes that the symptoms are isolated to the right lower extremity. She is seeking a management plan to improve her mobility and address these symptoms.

Review of Systems
The patient reports positive for lower extremity discomfort during exercise. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, or unintended weight loss. She denies any neurological deficits or changes in vision.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives in a single-story home with her spouse. She enjoys gardening and walking in her neighborhood. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Her mother had hypertension and a history of heart disease. Her father had a history of stroke.

Medication List
- Aspirin 81 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily

Vitals
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 132/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
Weight: 155 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 5.8%
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2
Total Cholesterol: 185 mg/dL
LDL: 98 mg/dL
HDL: 52 mg/dL
Triglycerides: 140 mg/dL

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical exam reveals skin and nail beds of the right foot are intact without any signs of breakdown. Pulses are palpable in the right foot. Capillary refill is less than 3 seconds in the right lower extremity. No visible signs of skin changes or breakdown are noted on the right leg.

Assessment
The patient has atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries with intermittent claudication. This is currently limited to the right leg.

Plan
1. Continue current medication regimen including aspirin and atorvastatin.
2. Encourage supervised exercise therapy to improve walking distance.
3. Follow up in three months to assess symptom progression.
4. Patient instructed to call the office if she experiences sudden worsening of symptoms or skin changes.

Electronically signed, E. Castillo, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the right leg with intermittent claudication (no HCC in V28): I70.211.

distractors.why: Rest pain is not documented (it would add HCC 264).
Atherosclerosis with claudication is documented: I70.21-.
